I confirmed this from the code at d99da09 in the codex-i3bf worktree. I did not rerun Docker because the code settles it.

1. pgrestore.py:274 reads nspacl in the "schemas" family, and compare() (lines 321-332) reports a family only when its rows differ. With M5 (nspacl replaced by null), the schemas row becomes nspname plus acldefault('n', nspowner). A schema ACL change then never shows up, whatever the privileges are.
2. Only one statement in tests/integration/backend/recovery/ changes a schema ACL: bk01g's `grant all on schema infrx to postgres` (test_restore.py:474). It is meant to compare equal, and it does whether or not M5 is applied. bk01g's revoke-to-empty damage is on the table infrx.t and expects {"relations"}.
3. bk01f's DAMAGE (lines 396-410) has no schemas entry. None of the other cases change a schema ACL or assert on "schemas differ". bk01/bk02 compare equal restores. bk01c widens relation ACLs through default privileges, and those never touch pg_namespace. bk01h checks has_schema_privilege directly, not through compare().
4. mutants_i3b.py lists only i3bm88 for schemas ('{}' in the coalesce), which bk01g kills in the equal direction. Nothing covers blindness to the ACL itself, and there is no "_schemas" family-removal mutant like i3bm62/63.

So restore.md A6 says schema ACLs are identical, and R92 says a real ACL difference is still named, including the schema equivalents. That invariant has no test that fails when it is broken. M5, or deleting the family outright, would pass test_restore.py. The reviewer's reported survivor matches this.

The production check is correct as written, so this is a test-coverage hole, not a restore defect. It is still blocking because the task's rubric counts an invariant with no killable test as blocking, and this one is the tenant-boundary schema grant.

Fix: add a bk01f DAMAGE entry, `"schemas": "grant usage on schema infrx to anon"`, and register a mutant that turns nspacl into null (or removes the family), killed by "bk01f and schemas".

I confirmed this from the code at d99da09. I did not run Docker because the mutant's survival follows from what the tests contain. The schemas family in pgrestore.py (CATALOG["schemas"], around line 274) is the only place a schema's nspacl is read. compare() reports it only as a "schemas differ" problem. In tests/integration/backend/recovery/ nothing expects that problem: a grep for "schemas differ", "schemas" or "on schema" finds only bk01g's `grant all on schema infrx to postgres`, and that is the equal direction (the owner's default spelled out, asserted == []). bk01f's DAMAGE dict (test_restore.py:396) covers policies, columns, functions, indexes, default_acls, triggers, functions_config and rows, with no schemas entry. bk01g's non-equal half revokes on table infrx.t and expects only {"relations"}. bk01c widens table grants and is named under relations. The registered schema mutant in mutants_i3b.py (~line 295) is `coalesce(nspacl, '{}', acldefault(...))`, which tests only the NULL-to-default direction. So swapping nspacl for null makes every schema compare as its owner's default, which makes compare() more lenient. No case can fail from that, since every case either expects equality or expects a different family, so the mutant survives. restore.md A6 lists "schema ACLs ... are identical" as part of the pass, and its R92 paragraph says an ACL emptied by a revoke "is still a difference", but for schemas no test can fail on that invariant. A restore that loses or widens USAGE on infrx or public for anon, authenticated or service_role would pass A6, and the tenant boundary depends on those grants. The gap goes back to 32f94b3, where the schemas family was added. The R92 follow-up rewrote this exact expression and registered only the equal-direction mutant. By the brief's criteria this is a restore-fidelity invariant with no killable test, so it is real and blocking. The suggested fix is small: add a schema-grant damage to bk01f, for example `grant usage on schema infrx to anon`, expect {"schemas"}, and register the nspacl->null mutant against bk01f.

nonblocking.claim_broken: The evidence (Limits 5) says the cause of #12's 24 spurious baseline-reds was not identified, and it treats the E runner's private TMPDIR as what makes concurrent runs safe.
nonblocking.evidence: D's pgharness keeps its per-port lock in tempfile.gettempdir(). E3B2's run_one gives every copy under tests/integration a private TMPDIR (root/tmp), so an I3B D-mode run (INFRX_I3B_PG=d, this lane's on_d) never shares the d3 lock. The container label is the same checkout, so a second run's ensure() `docker rm -f`s the first run's live container. Measured with two concurrent runner invocations on --only i3bm43/87/88/89. With a shared outer TMPDIR, run a had 4 baseline-red and run b 3 baseline-red. With private outer TMPDIRs, run a had 3 baseline-red plus i3bm43 'killed', and run b had 4 baseline-red. The outer TMPDIR makes no difference. Two plain pytest runs of -k bk01g behave differently. With the same TMPDIR the second gets 'HarnessBusy: another run holds …/infrx-d3-postgres-55434.lock' (the lock works). With distinct TMPDIRs both die: a with 'psycopg.OperationalError: … server closed the connection unexpectedly', b with 'ForeignContainer: refusing to remove infrx-d3-postgres-supabase: it does not exist'. The cause is therefore E's private-TMPDIR rule combined with this branch's D-mode path, not the list. It fails closed at the baseline (baseline-red) but fails open in the mutant phase: a container removed mid-mutant gives '1 failed', which the runner counts as killed. My solo full run showed no such effect.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: Keep the D harness lock shared for D-mode runs. In run_one, use `private = None` also when `os.environ.get("INFRX_I3B_PG") == "d"`, as E already does for apps/infrx-api suites 'because their port lock lives there'. Alternatively, have pgharness take its lock directory from an env var the runner passes through. Record the cause in Limits 5.

restore_lens_nonblocking.claim_broken: The lane says 'the fixture does not allow the plain image'. That is true in effect, but INFRX_I3B_PG=d with no INFRX_D1_IMAGE is not refused. The fixture carries plain-image code paths (lines 133 and 150: the _admin superuser branch and the NEEDS_SHIM shim apply), and they cannot work for 13 of the 24 cases. The failure is loud, but the configuration looks supported when it is not.
restore_lens_nonblocking.evidence: Reproduced exactly on d3 with the plain image: `5 failed, 10 passed, 1 skipped, 8 errors`. Every restore-dependent case (bk01_a/b/c/h, bk01f x8 via good_restore) stops at `pg_restore failed (1): ... unrecognized configuration parameter "transaction_timeout" / Command was: SET transaction_timeout = 0;`. The client that fails is the throwaway `infrx-i3b-pgclient-*` container from pgrestore.IMAGE: `pg_restore (PostgreSQL) 17.6`. The plain server is `postgres (PostgreSQL) 16.14`. The host's own pg_restore (16.15) is never used. So the lane's diagnosis is correct: a 17 client into a 16 server. bk02 fails at `psycopg.errors.UndefinedColumn: column "confirmed_at" of relation "users" does not exist`. HOSTED_SEED inserts into hosted/Supabase's auth.users.confirmed_at, and D's shim (supabase_shim.sql:58) has only email_confirmed_at. That is a shim schema difference, not a fixture bug.
restore_lens_nonblocking.minimal_fix: In needs_pg(), when ON_D and not d_harness().ON_SUPABASE, call pytest.fail('INFRX_I3B_PG=d needs INFRX_D1_IMAGE=supabase: pgrestore.IMAGE is a 17.6 client (transaction_timeout) and the shim has no auth.users.confirmed_at'). Delete the dead plain branches at lines 133 and 150. Use fail, not skip, so a plain run cannot go green without testing anything.

restore_lens_nonblocking.claim_broken: R92 says the check compares ACLs by the privileges they grant. Column privileges (pg_attribute.attacl) are in no family, and the project uses one: 0001_init.sql:208 `grant update (full_name, avatar_url) on public.profiles to authenticated`. This predates the lane and is not caused by the coalesce normalisation.
restore_lens_nonblocking.evidence: Against a good d3/Supabase restore, `revoke update (full_name) on public.profiles from authenticated` gives pg.compare == []. So does `grant update (full_name) on public.profiles to anon`, which is a widening. Both measured.
restore_lens_nonblocking.minimal_fix: Add a family: `select attrelid::regclass::text, attname, array(select unnest(attacl)::text order by 1)::text from pg_attribute where attrelid in (select c.oid from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace where n.nspname = any(%(s)s)) and attnum > 0 and not attisdropped and attacl is not null order by 1,2`. attacl has no owner default, so NULL needs no normalisation. Add a bk01f DAMAGE entry using the revoke above.
